answer: Like a reef that only grows where real currents feed it, an agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake locked for a long window and slashed if the identity misbehaves. A lone opal is cheap to fake, but a thousand fake identities each paying a stake and waiting out the lock becomes ruinously expensive, while honest agents earn the stake back plus fees. The lock turns identity from a free haven for sockpuppets into a costly commitment: attackers must fund every fake, wait, and risk losing it all, so mass forgery stops paying.
